artifacts.summary: Maps single-task Stages 2/2b/3b-hard/5a/5b/6/7 against the current batch engine (orchestrate-cycle-plan.sh, orchestrate-cycle-postflight.sh) for the four surviving WORK items (HARD, LOOP GUARD, AUXILIARY DISPATCHES, single-task routing flag), confirming orchestrate-churn.sh is a pure gap, identifying the per-task-cumulative vs. per-session loop-guard reconciliation as an open decision, flagging the fixed-agent/dispatch-row schema mismatch for aux dispatches, and confirming commands/orchestrate.md already has the branch point item (5) needs.

memory_candidates.content: In this repo's /orchestrate engine, single-task cycle_count is stored per-task-directory (.orchestrator-loop-guard) and is deliberately CUMULATIVE across /orchestrate re-invocations (never reset on a new session_id, protected by test-session-runtime-files.sh Case 3), while multi-task cycle_count lives in a per-session file (specs/.orchestrator-multi-state-${session_id}.json) that starts fresh every invocation. Any work that routes single-task runs through the multi-task path must explicitly decide whether to preserve the cumulative-budget guarantee or document its relaxation -- it is not automatically preserved.

orchestrate-churn.sh's target state file (.orchestrator-churn-state.json) is task-directory-scoped, not session-scoped -- verified via reap-session-runtime-files.sh and check-runtime-file-tracking.sh, which both classify it as a per-task runtime file requiring no session-based reaping. This makes churn/three-strikes state independent of whatever the loop-guard/session reconciliation decides, since the two state files answer different questions.

commands/orchestrate.md's STAGE 0 already branches cleanly on len(TASK_NUMBERS): ==1 falls through to the single-task Skill call, >1 builds waves_json/task_numbers_json/dep_graph_json and calls skill-orchestrate with multi_task_mode=true. Routing a single task number through the multi-task path only requires making the ==1 branch build the same trivial one-task inputs ([N], [[N]], {"N":[]}) and take the multi_task_mode=true path -- SKILL.md's own Stage 0 already dispatches correctly on that flag regardless of task count, so no new routing surface is needed.
